reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the cited text supports it: none of the quoted paragraphs (§6 documentation for charges, §8 Client covenants, §8(f) spamming controls, §9 Y2K access) creates an audit, inspection or usage-verification right running against the Client, so there is no frequency/notice/cost/system-access term to cap.
The redline is identical to the original and no comment was added, which is the expected output for a compliant finding — nothing is raised as a negotiation issue.

The failed deterministic check ('audit frequency limited') is a false signal here: the regex cannot match because the agreement contains no audit clause at all, which is a position better than the playbook's preferred outcome.

The rationale correctly distinguishes the two Client-side access items: §8(f) is TrueLink implementing controls on its own hosted environment, and §9 access is for TrueLink-funded Y2K repairs at Client's request — neither is an audit right or unbounded access to Customer systems triggering the walk-away.
